summary: Documentation only. (1) The README status line (EN/DE) no longer names router and agent versions, which had gone stale (0.23.0/0.30.0); it points to the releases and the top CHANGELOG row instead, so it cannot go stale again. (2) docs/operations.md and its German twin gain a 'What to back up' section before 'Restoring a backup', derived from the code: config folder (/etc/skirnir-router: config.yaml, certs/ or tls/, agent/ release folder; agentupdate.agent_dir, ops.manifest_path, router-layout.sh), the secret source rather than the rendered secrets.env (render-env.sh, install-router docs), the state folder files written via common.state_dir / Config._locate (nodes.json from app.py, roles.yaml, deletions.jsonl, usage.json incl. monthly cloud spend, metrics.json, perf.json, events.jsonl, requests.jsonl, ollama-latest.json; same list as router-layout.sh STATE_FILES), the optional PostgreSQL session database and outbox, the external memory backend, the audit log, the agent configuration and identity.dir (agent-identity.key and provisioned.json, DPAPI LOCAL_MACHINE on Windows per platform_windows.go) and the operator's update signing key folder (deploy/agent_keys.py). The 'Restoring a backup' intro now says deletions.jsonl lives in router.state_dir (since ADR-0086), not next to config.yaml. Security-relevant content of the text: it tells operators to back up the secret source rather than secrets.env, to protect the backup of the secret-store access file like the file itself, and to keep the signing-key backup offline and encrypted; it keeps the existing advice that deletions.jsonl must not be restored older than the database (TM-12). It discloses no secret, endpoint, host or credential, and names only default paths that the install scripts and existing docs already publish. No code, configuration, version, workflow or review-policy change.

tests.evidence: security_relevant false; changed paths README.md, README.de.md, docs/operations.md, docs/operations.de.md.

limitations: Documentation only; no behaviour changed, so no negative test applies.
The backup list was derived from origin/main at fb19cb6; parallel open PRs (secrets renderer, status sinks) may change the secret source or add state files, and would then update this section.

TM-15's next action 'backup controls for these files' is only partly addressed: the list names the files and how to protect sensitive backups, but Skirnir still has no backup tooling, retention or integrity check of its own; the risk register is unchanged.
